Playbook.name: F5 WAF — Targeted Web-Attack Campaign Against Internet Banking - SOC Playbook

Reference.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application
F5 BIG-IP ASM / Advanced WAF violation rating and enforcement

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: One source drove a multi-vector web-attack campaign against JCB internet banking — a threshold volume of events across many exploit classes (SQLi, XSS, Command Execution, Server Side Code Injection, Path Traversal, RFI, HTTP Request Smuggling, Session Hijacking, Detection Evasion, Trojan/Backdoor/Spyware, JSON Parser Attack, Injection Attempt). This rule casts a wider net than the critical-reached and RCE analytics: it fires on breadth and volume regardless of rating or enforcement. The triage question is two-part: how effective was enforcement (mostly blocked = contained attempt; substantial not-blocked = exposure), and did any high-rating request reach a banking backend?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: A concerted multi-vector campaign against internet banking signals deliberate targeting rather than opportunistic scanning. Even if the WAF blocks most of it, one class slipping through can lead to data theft, account/transaction manipulation, or a DMZ foothold — and the source is a candidate for edge blocking and threat-intel enrichment.

Assets.AssetType: F5 BIG-IP ASM / Advanced WAF fronting JCB internet banking and public web apps (verified live: appliance F5-FRNT-WAF-01.JCBank.com.jo)
Published internet-banking applications and their backend servers

LogSources.LogSource: F5 ASM CEF events via syslog - logs-cef.log-* (observer.vendor == "F5"; verified live)

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: F5 ASM logging to CEF over syslog, parsed into logs-cef.log-* (verified live).

CEF fields (verified live populated for F5): cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4 = attack type; cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber2 = violation rating; cef.extensions.deviceCustomString1 = ASM policy; url.original = request URL; http.request.method = method; cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber1 = backend HTTP response; cef.extensions.deviceAction = passed | alerted | blocked; source.geo.country_name and source.as.organization.name = attribution.

Signal.Name: Multi-vector campaign volume
Signal.Details: observer.vendor F5 with a threshold volume from one source.ip across the exploit-class set in cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4 (SQL-Injection, Cross Site Scripting (XSS), Command Execution, Server Side Code Injection, Path Traversal, Remote File Include, HTTP Request Smuggling Attack, Session Hijacking, Detection Evasion, Trojan/Backdoor/Spyware, JSON Parser Attack, Injection Attempt).

Signal.Name: Enforcement effectiveness
Signal.Details: The blocked-versus-not-blocked balance (cef.extensions.deviceAction) reveals whether the campaign was contained or partially forwarded.

Input.name: $source_ip
Input.description: Attacking source IP from the alert (source.ip, threshold group key). Primary investigation pivot.

ImmediateCapture.Item: Breadth: how many distinct exploit classes (cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4) and the peak rating (cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber2)
Targeted banking apps / policies (cef.extensions.deviceCustomString1) and the blocked-versus-not-blocked balance (cef.extensions.deviceAction)

InitialAssessment.Rule: If enforcement blocked essentially everything (INV-01 dominated by action = blocked), this is a contained targeted campaign — still a True Positive for tracking/blocking, but not an active breach.
If a meaningful share is not-blocked at rating 4-5 (INV-02) — especially with a backend HTTP response in INV-03 — escalate as bypassed enforcement / possible reached-target.
If $source_ip is an authorised internal scanner / pentest host on schedule, lean False Positive (authorised) after confirming the engagement window and that nothing reached the backend.

Investigation.Goal: Characterise the campaign from $source_ip: which exploit classes and how broad, how effective enforcement was, which banking apps were targeted, and whether any high-rating unblocked request reached a backend.

Step.name: Attack-class breadth and enforcement mix for this source
Step.Purpose: Show the full spread of exploit classes and, for each, whether the WAF blocked, alerted or passed — the contained-versus-exposed picture.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "F5" AND source.ip == "$source_ip" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS events = COUNT(*), max_rating = MAX(cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber2) BY cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4, cef.extensions.deviceAction | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 40
Step.AnalystNotes: Many distinct attack types from one source = deliberate multi-vector targeting. If the action column is overwhelmingly "blocked", the WAF contained the campaign (track and block the source). Rows where action is passed/alerted at max_rating 4-5 are the exposure — carry those classes into INV-02 and INV-03. Ignore high-volume N/A "passed" rows: those are ordinary application traffic, not attacks.

Step.name: Which banking apps were targeted and how hard
Step.Purpose: Rank the ASM policies (banking apps) this source hit at rating 4-5, with the count of not-blocked events and the strongest backend response seen — where the real exposure sits.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "F5" AND source.ip == "$source_ip" AND cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber2 >= 4 AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS events = COUNT(*), attack_types = COUNT_DISTINCT(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4), not_blocked = COUNT(CASE(cef.extensions.deviceAction != "blocked", 1, null)), max_response = MAX(cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber1) BY cef.extensions.deviceCustomString1 | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: A policy with high events, several distinct attack_types and a non-zero not_blocked is the most exposed banking app. max_response above 0 (a real HTTP code) on a not-blocked policy is a reached-target hint — confirm with INV-03. Policies are the JCB banking apps (e.g. /Common/JCBank-Website-Policy, /Common/HQ-Web-Mobile-ICS-Policy, /Common/MenaMobile-WAF_Auto).

Step.name: High-rating unblocked requests that may have reached a backend
Step.Purpose: Pull the exact rating-4/5 unblocked requests with URL, method, backend response and geo — the reached-target and payload evidence.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "F5" AND source.ip == "$source_ip" AND cef.extensions.deviceAction != "blocked" AND cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber2 >= 4 AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4, http.request.method, url.original, cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber1, cef.extensions.deviceCustomString1, source.geo.country_name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: Empty result here is the good outcome: no high-rating request escaped enforcement. Rows present mean specific exploit requests were forwarded — a backend response (cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber1) of 2xx/3xx/5xx on any of them is a reached-target signal; inspect url.original for the payload and scope the app behind cef.extensions.deviceCustomString1.

Node.Condition: INV-03 shows a high-rating unblocked request with a backend HTTP response (cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber1 of 2xx/3xx/5xx) against a banking policy — part of the campaign reached the application.
Node.Result: True Positive (Campaign Reached Application - escalate to IR; inspect the targeted banking app/DB)

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows broad multi-vector targeting of internet banking from an external source (INV-03 foreign geo / hosting ASN), whether or not enforcement blocked it — a deliberate campaign against JCB.
Node.Result: True Positive (Targeted Multi-Vector Campaign - block the source at the edge, enrich with threat intel; escalate if any not-blocked at rating 4-5)

Node.Condition: INV-01/INV-03 confirm $source_ip is a documented internal scanner / contracted-pentest host on an authorised schedule AND nothing reached the backend.
Node.Result: False Positive (Authorised vulnerability scan / penetration test - exception the tester for the engagement window only)

Node.Condition: Volume is dominated by benign application traffic mislabeled by an over-eager or staging signature, or by an ASM policy in transparent mode inflating passed/alerted counts, rather than genuine attacks.
Node.Result: Misconfiguration (Over-eager staging signature or transparent policy - engage the WAF team to tune/enforce)

Node.Condition: External multi-vector campaign, but backend reach cannot be confirmed or refuted from available fields and the source is not an authorised tester.

FalsePositive.Definition: Authorised vulnerability scanning or penetration testing that legitimately exercises many exploit classes against the web apps — an approved activity, not benign background noise.

Indicators.Item: Internal or contracted-pentest source on a documented, in-window engagement.
Broad but uniform coverage typical of a tool; INV-03 shows nothing reached the backend.
Source attributes to a known testing host/range, not a foreign hosting provider.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the engagement window and tester source with the owning team.
Exception the tester source for the engagement duration only.
Close as false_positive with the ticket reference attached.

TruePositive.Definition: A deliberate multi-vector web-attack campaign against JCB internet banking, whether contained by the WAF or partially forwarded.

Indicators.Item: Many distinct exploit classes from one external source (INV-01).
Multiple banking policies targeted at rating 4-5 (INV-02).
Any not-blocked high-rating requests, especially with a backend response (INV-03).

SOCAction.Item: Block $source_ip at the WAF/edge; enrich the IP and ASN with threat intel and check for related sources.
If anything reached the backend, escalate to IR and inspect the targeted banking app and its data stores.
Preserve requests and matched signatures; consider virtual-patching the classes seen.

Misconfiguration.Definition: Event volume is inflated by an over-eager/staging signature or a transparent ASM policy rather than genuine attacks, producing a campaign-shaped alert from mostly benign traffic.

Indicators.Item: The bulk of events resolve to a single immature signature or transparent policy.
Payloads on inspection are legitimate application requests.

SOCAction.Item: Engage the WAF team to tune the offending signature or move the policy to enforcement.
Re-triage as True Positive if genuine high-rating attacks are found within the volume.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Assess breadth and enforcement from INV-01; determine whether the campaign was contained (mostly blocked) or partially forwarded.
Check INV-03 for any high-rating unblocked request with a backend response; if present, engage IR for the targeted banking app.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Block $source_ip at the WAF/edge; enrich the IP/ASN and hunt for related campaign sources hitting the same policies.
For any reached-target, inspect the banking app and DB behind the targeted policy; preserve request forensics.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Ensure internet-banking ASM policies are enforcing; virtual-patch the exploit classes observed in the campaign.
Feed the source/ASN to edge blocklists and threat-intel; review whether a rate/geo control is warranted for the targeted apps.

Escalation.Trigger: Any high-rating unblocked request with a backend response, a broad external multi-vector campaign against banking apps, or evidence of a coordinated set of sources.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Authorised scan/pentest confirmed against $source_ip; INV-03 shows no backend reach; engagement ticket attached.
Outputs of INV-01, INV-02, INV-03 attached to the case.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Source blocked and enriched; any reached-target app inspected and cleared or remediated.
Campaign breadth, enforcement effectiveness and virtual-patch actions documented.
